If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Community Development

 AGENDA  2
REGULAR MEETING OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION
Wednesday, June 5, 2019

  NEW BUSINESS

  LOCATION:  2817 MONTROSE AVENUE
   APPEAL OF DENSITY BONUS HOUSING PLAN CASE NO. PDBP 1823423

  APPLICANT:  Garo Minassian, Architect, Inc.
  ZONE:  “R-1650” – Medium High Density Residential Zone
  LEGAL DESCRIPTION: Lots 3 and 4 in Tract 2718, in the City of Glendale, in the
  County of Los Angeles

  APPELLANTS:  - Glendale Homeowners Coordinating Council,
  - Montrose/Sparr Heights/Verdugo City Homeowners
  Association
  - Montrose Villas Homeowners Association

  STAFF:  Vilia Zemaitaitis

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION
  Appeal of Planning Hearing Officer’s approval of two incentives (additional height &
  reduced setbacks) and two waivers (additional FAR & increased lot coverage), per
  Government Code Section 65915 & GMC 30.36, in order to construct a new 3-story,
  38-unit, multi-family affordable housing project on the 36,000 square-foot lot, zoned
  R-1650. The applicant is providing 10.7% very low income units (three units total) for
  a 32.5% density bonus by right for an additional 10 units over the 28 units permitted
  by right in the R-1650 zone for lots greater than 90 feet. The project qualifies for
  reduced parking inclusive of guest and handicapped spaces, tandem spaces, and at-
  grade parking under the State Density Bonus Law and GMC 30.36.090. Development
  of the project requires the demolition of the existing church structures and also Design
  Review Board approval. The existing Oak tree and river rock wall along Montrose
  Avenue are to be preserved and maintained.

  PLANNING HEARING OFFICER’S APPROVAL
  Concessions or Incentives, pursuant to GMC 30.36.070.A
  (1) Increased maximum height to 56 feet (three stories permitted by right).
  (2) Decreased minimum required interior setbacks:
  • Minimum interior setback of five feet and average of six feet along the east,
  minimum interior setback of six feet and average of 14 feet along the north, and
  minimum interior setback of five feet and average of 16 feet along the west for
  all floors.

  Waivers or Modifications of Development Standards, pursuant to GMC 30.36.070.A
  (1) Increased maximum allowable floor area ratio (FAR) to 1.14 (living area only) / 1.78
  (including at-grade garage).
  (2) Increased maximum allowable lot coverage to 53% (living area only) / 74%
  (including garage).
 AGENDA  3
REGULAR MEETING OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION
Wednesday, June 5, 2019

  CODE REQUIRES
  Concessions (Incentives)
  (1) Maximum building height and stories of 36 feet for a flat roof and three stories
  (GMC 30.11.030)
  (2) Minimum interior setbacks (GMC 30.11.030):
  • Five foot minimum and eight foot average for the first residential floor, eight foot
  minimum and 11-foot average for the second residential floor, and 11-foot
  minimum and 14-foot average for the third residential floor.

  Modification of Development Standards (Waivers)
  (1) Maximum floor area ratio (FAR) of 1.0 in the R-1650 zone (GMC 30.11.030).
  (2) Maximum lot coverage of 50% (GMC 30.11.030).

  ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
  The project is exempt from CEQA review as a Class 32 “In-fill Development Projects”
  exemption pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines Section 15332 because the Project
  meets all the conditions for an in-fill development project.

  REQUESTED ACTION
  Community Development Department staff recommends that the Planning
  Commission sustain the Planning Hearing Officer’s decision to approve Density
  Bonus Housing Plan Case No. PDBP 1823423 for 2817 Montrose Avenue as stated
  in the staff report dated June 5, 2019.

  STAFF

  ~  Staff member Vilia Zemaitaitis, overviewed the project. She added that this
  project "Density Bonus Housing Plan" was heard by the Planning Hearing Officer
  and was approved with conditions. The decision of the Planning Hearing Officer
  was appealed by three homeowners associations to the Planning Commission.

  3
 Planning Commission Minutes
June 5, 20 19

  Ms. Zemaitaitis apprised the Planning Commissioners that after giving a closer
  look at the "Parking Exception" which was approved as part of this project, and
  after consultation with legal staff, it was concluded that this agenda item be
  remanded back to the Planning Hearing Officer for a new hearing.

  Ms. Zemaitaitis stated that the City Attorney's office informed her a few hours
  before the Planning Commission hearing today, that this appeal cannot be heard
  by the Planning Commission . This agenda item will be remanded back to the
  Planning Hearing Officer to again review the 'at grade parking' issue and if it
  meets zoning code.

  ~  Ms. Gillian Van Muyden, Chief Assistant City Attorney, informed the Planning
  Commissioners, that since this agenda item was advertised and noticed in the
  paper and public notices mailed out to owners and occupants within a 500-foot
  radius , it is proper that the Planning Commissioners hear testimony from the
  public who are present today.

  APPELLANT
  - Mr. Grant Michals, President of the Glendale Homeowners Co-ordinating Council
  and the President of Montrose-Verdugo City Sparr Heights Neighborhood
  Association , and one of the co-appellants of the appeal. He said that he is in
  opposition to this proposed project, because the discretionary waivers and
  modifications granted to the developer are excessive and the proposed project will
  be massive and out of scale with the surrounding neighborhood.

  APPLICANT
  - Garo Minassian, architect on the project and representing the applicant, stated
  that a few hours before the Planning Commission hearing today, planning division
  staff informed him that the appeal hearing on '2817 Montrose Avenue' will not be
  heard today, as recommended by the City's City Attorney's Office.

  Their concerns were:
  o All resident parking in the 'R-1650 ' zone be in an enclosed subterranean or
  semi-subterranean parking garage.
  o The at-grade parking garage is not allowed by Code.

  DISCUSSION BY PLANNING COMMISSIONERS
  Upon questioning by the Planning Commissioners, Ms. Zemaitaitis stated that if the
  Planning Commission remands this agenda item to the Planning Hearing Officer, the
  new public notice will be renoticed in the newspaper for a new hearing date, and new
  public notices will be mailed out to all the owners and occupants in the area residing
  within a 500-foot radius, as required by Code.

  Planning Commissioners requested that Ms.Van Muyden from the City Attorney's
  office provide details and reasoning as to remanding this agenda item to the Planning
  Hearing Officer. Ms. Van Muyden reiterated that Planning Division staff will look
  closely at the 'at-grade parking garage' issue.

  After much discussion, the Planning Commissioners made the following motion.
